result:
`is_supported_version` now returns `False` when `set_min_proto_version` or `set_max_proto_version` raises `SSL.Error`, instead of letting it propagate. I haven't run the tests, per your instructions.

**The fix** is in `mitmproxy/net/tls.py`. I moved the whole setup into the existing `try`: context creation, cipher list, both protocol-version setters, connection creation and `set_connect_state()`. The `recv()` probe stays where it was. The existing `except SSL.WantReadError` / `except SSL.Error` handlers now cover setup errors as well. I also added a short comment explaining why the setters sit inside the `try`. Versions that were already supported behave as before.

**The test** is `test_supported_setup_error` in `test/mitmproxy/net/test_tls.py`. It monkeypatches `SSL.Context.set_min_proto_version` to raise `SSL.Error` and asserts that `is_supported_version(SSL3)` returns `False`. It clears the `@cache` before and after, so the result isn't served from a cached value and doesn't leak into other tests. It should fail without the fix on any OpenSSL build.
